summary: Aurenet: dedicated pool mis-registration caused cross-variant routing, streaming truncation, and billing exposure
description:
Issue summary:
Aurenet observed a major outage impacting their dedicated pool (prod-us-west) starting 2026-03-09 22:12 UTC. High rates of 5xx responses and streaming truncations were reported; several long-running requests retried and incurred unexpected token billing.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency/5xx spike: ~12% of requests for Aurenet returned 5xx over a 24-minute window.
- Streaming truncation: several streaming sessions cut mid-response, clients reopened sockets and retried.
- Billing exposure: retries and duplicate completions caused an estimated ~8% increase in token usage for the affected window.
- Affected endpoints: text-generation streaming and chat endpoints pinned to redwood-4x-13b variants.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 22:12 UTC: Aurenet support reported increased 500s and truncated streams via in-app alert and support portal.
- 22:15 UTC: On-call SRE acknowledged; incident declared.
- 22:20-22:30 UTC: Initial mitigation: traffic rate-limited and canary routing toggled to reduce burst to dedicated pool.
- 22:31 UTC: Temporary routing to fp16 variant applied for sessions > 1024 tokens.
- 22:45 UTC: Hotfix for scheduler rolled out; node compatibility tags corrected; traffic restored gradually.
- 23:05 UTC: Monitoring indicated error rate returning to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Send a streaming request with sequence length > 1024 to the customer-dedicated endpoint.
2) Observe early stream termination and a follow-up retry that produces an additional completion.
3) Check request logs in console for mixed kernel selection warnings.

Investigation notes:
- Root cause: During a rolling node upgrade to rotate a GPU driver on the dedicated pool, several worker nodes registered with the scheduler missing the "variant_compat" tag that declares whether they can safely run the quantized kernel. Smart-routing's affinity rules treated those nodes as compatible, so requests for the quantized model were scheduled onto workers that actually used an incompatible kernel build.
- Compatibility mismatch led to intermittent kernel selection failures at runtime. For short requests the fallback succeeded; for longer streaming sessions the runtime truncated the stream and returned a 5xx. Retries sometimes completed on the fallback variant producing duplicate completions.
- Contributing factor: Canary checks did validate node liveness and driver version, but the preflight did not validate the node's declared capability tag.
- Observability gaps: console did emit a low-level kernel mismatch log, but it was not surfaced as an alert to the dedicated pool owner or an automated circuit-breaker.

Mitigation applied:
- Immediate: Re-routed heavy/long-tail traffic to fp16 variant for Aurenet (22:31 UTC) and enabled two-minute request de-duplication at the ingress for the dedicated pool.
- Short-term fix (22:45 UTC): Deployed scheduler hotfix to re-evaluate and enforce node "variant_compat" on re-registration; evicted mis-registered nodes and drained traffic.
- Customer communication: Sent an interim status update at 22:50 UTC explaining mitigation and that we were investigating root cause.

Resolution summary:
- Root cause patch merged and rolled to prod (PRs linked).
- Aurenet traffic drained to compatible nodes; error rates returned to baseline by 23:05 UTC.
- Customer credited for excess tokens equivalent to the estimated 8% exposure and offered a 30-day trial of Dedicated monitoring add-on.

Post-incident action items (owner / ETA):
- Update serving runtime canary checklist to include validation of node capability tags (OWNER: infra-team, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Add a console alert when kernel-compatibility warnings appear (OWNER: console-team, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Implement automated rollback of node registration if capability tags are missing (OWNER: scheduler-team, ETA: 2026-03-25).
- Run a dedicated pool chaos exercise focused on node re-registration (OWNER: SRE, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- Postmortem write-up and share with customer and internal stakeholders (OWNER: support, ETA: 2026-03-14).

resolution: Hotfix deployed to scheduler to enforce node capability tags; mis-registered nodes evicted and traffic rerouted to compatible fp16 variant; customer credited for excess tokens; runbook and console alerts updated.
resolution_notes:
- PRs merged: serving-runtime kernel-compat logs improved (PR #6789) and scheduler registration enforcement (PR #312).
- Billing credited on 2026-03-10; finance ticket INT-34021 created to track credit reconciliation.
- Runbook updated and stored at linked Confluence page.
- Follow-up: schedule inter-team postmortem review 2026-03-16 (attendees: support, SRE, scheduler, serving-runtime, customer success).
